learning: Iteration 10 reproduced iteration 7 exactly (303.79), so the simulator is deterministic for this design. The ±0.07 m span and the 12 mm footprint both removed oval completions, and the 0.6 kg light-robot setting is the only one that completes. Slalom line loss (0.3 per run) and the s-bend and slalom off-track failures remain unresolved; they are the first things to address if more iterations existed.
notes: Final package: the iteration 7 and 10 platform and controller, unchanged, so the final race uses the only configuration with proven oval completions (14 of 20, score 303.8). The sensor weights are about 33.3 times x, matching the ±0.06 m span. Gains and line-loss rule are identical to the reproduced run.
rationale: This is the final iteration, so the robot raced here is the one the unseen-track evaluation will use. The evidence favours keeping the platform and controller that already produced results. Iteration 7 and its unchanged re-run in iteration 10 both scored 303.79 with 14 of 20 oval completions, which shows the race is deterministic for this design. Iterations 8 (12 mm footprint) and 9 (±0.07 m span, unscaled weights) both dropped oval completions to 0, and those are the only controller-relevant variants tested, so neither is carried forward. I therefore keep the iteration 7 geometry exactly: seven 16 mm sensors at y = 0.02 m, x = ±0.06 m, 0.10 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.6 kg, 0.12 m body. The controller is also unchanged: kp 2.2, kd 0.5, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.4, last_direction, and weights of about 33.3 times x (±2 at the outer sensors). Gains were lowered from kp 2.5 and raised in kd during the light-robot runs (iterations 2 to 3, which gave oscillation 0.27 to 0.31), and this combination is the only one that produced oval completions. Untested changes to gain, weight scale or track would risk the oval completions, which carry most of the score, and I cannot verify them before the final race. Expected, not measured: oval completion near 70 percent on a similar track, with the s-bend and slalom still likely to end off track.
